naslov: From the Well to the Palace: Yusuf's Journey to Deliverance

segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: We continue with the tafsir (exegesis) of Surah Yusuf. When Yusuf's brothers had agreed and thrown Yusuf into the well, Yusuf remained in that well for three days.

The whole time he was in the well, his brothers watched over all of it and kept an eye on it. Why? So that no caravan would come, or no one would come who might pull him out of the well and then ask whose he was and where he lived, and then take him back to his family.

That would have been a great disgrace for them, and they would surely have provoked the anger of their people, because Ya'qub was a prophet, respected among his people. So they kept watch the whole time.
And they threw him into a well by which caravans usually passed. Because, according to the plan of one of the brothers – when they had agreed to kill him, he said: "No, I have another solution.

Let us throw him into a well by which caravans pass; the caravans will take him and carry him off somewhere far from his father." And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَجَاءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَى دَلْوَهُ" – and a caravan came, a caravan came to the well, and they sent their water-drawer, the water-drawer, to fetch water. When this water-drawer came to the well, he let the bucket down to the bottom of the well,

and Yusuf caught hold of the bucket, and he pulled him out. "Qala ya bushra hadha ghulam" – he said: "Good news, here is a boy!" Which indicates that Yusuf was small, because otherwise, had he been big, he could not have pulled him up with that bucket. What further indicates that Yusuf was small are the words of Ya'qub, when he says: "I fear that a wolf will eat him." He did not say: "I fear that a wolf will eat you,"

because his brothers were grown up and could defend themselves, while Yusuf was, Yusuf was small. Also, when his brothers said: "Send him with us," they said, "let him play a little, let him enjoy himself" – and that is for children, not for grown men. So all of this indicates that Yusuf was very small, that Yusuf was very small. What did this water-drawer do? "Wa asarruhu bida'ah" – He says: these water-drawers tried to hide him, so that he would be part of their merchandise, as some mufassirun,

the commentators of the Qur'an, say: they wanted to hide him from the rest of the caravan, because he was very beautiful; they saw that he was a very beautiful boy, and they, of course, also wanted to sell him. So, it is said, they tried to hide him from the rest of the caravan. And at that point Yusuf's brothers arrive, who are watching over all of this. Now, Yusuf's brothers do not know that these men also want to sell him, to hide him, to count him among their merchandise and then sell him, so they play it safe,

they play it safe, so that he would not somehow find his way back to his father. And they said: "That is our runaway slave" – Yusuf's brothers said this about Yusuf: "That is our slave; he ran away, fled from us." And they asked Yusuf: "Are you our slave?" Yusuf, in fear – what is he to do?
He is afraid that if he says "I am not, I am their brother," they will take him back, and they would surely kill him. So he says: "Yes, I am their slave. Yes, I am their, their slave."
So they offered him, as the Qur'an tells us, and He says: these brothers sold him, Yusuf, for a pittance, for a few dirhams.
And, He says, they did not ask for much. They sold him to these water-drawers for a pittance. They did not ask for much, because what was their goal, after all? Only to get rid of Yusuf.
And here, dear brothers, Yusuf's story in Palestine comes to an end. So, his story in Palestine lasts up to this point. After his brothers sold him, the caravan took him to Egypt.
And there they sold him to the governor of Egypt, or, let us say, the prime minister, because he was the second man of Egypt.

And when this prime minister brought him to his palace, he said, as the Qur'an informs us… And when this prime minister brought him to his palace, having bought him – and how could it not be this prime minister who bought him, since these men, that is, these water-drawers, were probably looking for someone wealthy to buy him – for how could he not buy him,

when the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), says: "Utiya Yusufu shatral-husni" – Yusuf was given half of all beauty. What does that mean? Half of beauty was given to Yusuf, and the other half of beauty was distributed among other people. So imagine how beautiful Yusuf was, and surely they were looking for someone distinguished, someone with the money to buy him.
And when he brought him to his house, that is, to the palace, he said to his wife: "Make his stay pleasant. Treat him well. Give him everything he needs."

Why? He says, he says: "Perhaps he will be of some benefit to us, aw nattakhidhahu waladan – or we will adopt him as a son," that is, we will take him as our child. Why? This man probably had no children, so he wanted to adopt him, so that he would be his son. So this governor of Egypt saw something in Yusuf that others did not see. Ibn Mas'ud, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu – a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, the most learned companion of the Prophet – says: "Afrasun-nasi thalathah" – he says: the most perceptive, or the three most perceptive

people are: in first place, he says, this governor of Egypt. Why? Because, he says, he saw in Yusuf what others did not see, and so he said to his wife: "Treat him well; perhaps he will benefit us tomorrow, or we will adopt him as a son."

And Yusuf, as you will see later, benefited the whole of Egypt and all the surrounding countries. In second place, as Ibn Mas'ud says, is the daughter of Shu'ayb. When Musa, having fled from Pharaoh, arrived in Madyan, the city of Shu'ayb, and watered the cattle, or livestock, of Shu'ayb's daughters, who could not get to the spring – and Musa is known for his strength, so he took the livestock and watered them – this daughter of his, when she saw how

strong he was, how trustworthy he was, how humble he was, said: "Ya abatista'jirhu" – she said: "O father," she said, "hire him – inna khayra manista'jartal-qawiyyul-amin" – she said: "for the best one you can hire is the one who is strong and trustworthy," referring to Musa, alayhis-salam. And Musa, alayhis-salam, later benefited the Children of Israel, that is, he delivered them from Pharaoh.

And in third place, he says, Abu Bakr: the third most perceptive person, he says, is Abu Bakr, when he appointed Umar as caliph. And we know who Umar was, and what Umar was, and how much he benefited, benefited the ummah.

So we see that this governor of Egypt ordered that Yusuf be treated well, well, treated well, and that his stay in Egypt be made pleasant, pleasant. Also, among the blessings with which Allah favoured Yusuf is that this governor of Egypt did not place him with the other servants, but gave him a special place in the palace, a special place in the palace. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: and just as We
caused Yusuf to see the dream, and after that caused his brothers to throw him into the well, and after that caused this governor of Egypt to buy him, so We will give Yusuf power in the land.
And We will teach him the interpretation of dreams. And we will see later how Yusuf interprets dreams, how Yusuf interprets dreams. The interpretation of dreams, dear brothers, is a whole science.

But it is also a gift from Allah. Not everyone can interpret dreams. Someone may be learned but have no, no talent for interpreting dreams. So the interpretation of dreams is a gift from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. "Wa li nu'allimahu min ta'wilil-ahadith, wallahu ghalibun 'ala amrihi" – He says: and Allah does what He wills,

and His command must be carried out. "Wa lakinna aktharan-nasi la ya'lamun" – but, He says, most people do not know the wisdom of why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, did with Yusuf what He did: from being thrown into the well, to then living in the palace of this powerful man, and so on, and so forth. Most people do not know why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, gives something, a certain thing; they do not know… we do not know the wisdom, just as we do not know the wisdom of what is happening today in Palestine, in Gaza.

We do not know what the wisdom is, what lies behind it. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will reveal it, in sha Allah, in sha Allah soon. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to help us and to forgive our sins. In sha Allah, tomorrow we continue with this wonderful, beautiful story. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to reward you with every good. As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi ta'ala.
